metadata.case_name: CHAN SIU YOUN v. NG KAM MAN AND OTHERS

injuries.description: Cervical acceleration-deceleration injury (cervical whiplash) with degenerative change at C5-6 resulting in sprain neck and residual neck pain
source: the plaintiff was admitted into that hospital on 25 May 1996 for his sprain neck injury sustained in the traffic accident.
Mr Chan's history, physical findings and X-ray findings suggest a cervical acceleration-deceleration injury or commonly known as cervical whiplash.
At this examination, X-ray revealed degenerative changes at C5-6 level of the cervical spine, which was very likely to be the cause of the persistent neck pain.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

manifestations.description: on and off residual neck pain
difficulty to perform long hours of overhead ceiling work due to neck pain on prolonged neck extension
required physiotherapy and follow-up treatment; unable to resume full duties and took lighter duty work (delivery assistant)

losses.description: Neck injury with residual neck pain affecting bodily function
Unable to carry on internal decoration business immediately after accident; took on lighter delivery work and cannot perform long hours of overhead ceiling work
